record.paper_title: On an Open Question in Recovering Sturm--Liouville-Type Operators with Delay
record.original_question: For Robin-type variants of the delayed Sturm-Liouville inverse spectral problem, where the boundary conditions y(0)=y^(j)(pi)=0 are replaced by y'(0)-h y(0)=y^(j)(pi)=0 with complex h, determine whether an iso-bispectral counterexample analogous to the one constructed for y(0)=y^(j)(pi)=0 can be built, or whether the two spectra continue to determine the potential q uniquely in the corresponding delay ranges.

evidence.quote: Instead of (\ref{2}), one could alternatively impose the boundary conditions $y'(0)-hy(0)=y^{(j)}(\pi)=0$ with a complex parameter $h,$ which can be found given the input data of Inverse Problem~1.
Some discussion on a possibility of constructing a similar counterexample for other types of boundary conditions is provided, and new open questions are outlined.

However, the main difference from the case of boundary conditions (\ref{2}) is that, in the case of (\ref{rob}), there is no relation analogous to (\ref{3.6.1}). In other words, the constant $\omega$ is not determined by the function $w_1(x).$ Thus, each characteristic function (\ref{3.3}) and (\ref{3.4}) could depend on $\alpha$ even if $w_1(x)$ did not. So the presented scheme does not refute the uniqueness theorem in~\cite{Yur20}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Sturm–Liouville-type differential equation with constant delay
\[
-y''(x) + q(x)\,y(x-a) = \lambda\, y(x), \qquad x \in (0,\pi),
\]
where the delay parameter satisfies $a \in [\pi/3, \pi)$, the complex-valued potential $q \in L_2(0,\pi)$ is supported on $[a,\pi]$, and $q(x)=0$ for $x\in[0,a)$ (so that the term $q(x)y(x-a)$ is interpreted with $y$ extended appropriately on $(-a,0)$).

For $j\in\{0,1\}$ and a fixed complex number $h\in\mathbb{C}$, let $\sigma_j(q,h)$ denote the spectrum (counted with multiplicity) of the boundary value problem
\[
-y''(x) + q(x)\,y(x-a) = \lambda\, y(x), \qquad y'(0) - h\,y(0) = 0,\quad y^{(j)}(\pi) = 0.
\]
Thus $\sigma_0(q,h)$ corresponds to the boundary condition $y(\pi)=0$ and $\sigma_1(q,h)$ to $y'(\pi)=0$.

Inverse spectral problem. Given $h\in\mathbb{C}$ and the two spectra $\sigma_0(q,h)$ and $\sigma_1(q,h)$, is the potential $q$ uniquely determined?

Question. Decide which of the following holds for $a$ in the range $[\pi/3, 2\pi/5)$ (and, more generally, for the delay ranges in $[\pi/3,\pi)$ where non-uniqueness is known to fail or to hold in the Dirichlet case $y(0)=y^{(j)}(\pi)=0$):

(a) Construct an explicit pair of distinct potentials $q_1,q_2 \in L_2(0,\pi)$ (with the support assumption above) and a value $h\in\mathbb{C}$ such that
\[
\sigma_0(q_1,h) = \sigma_0(q_2,h) \quad\text{and}\quad \sigma_1(q_1,h) = \sigma_1(q_2,h),
\]
i.e., an iso-bispectral counterexample for the Robin-type boundary conditions; or

(b) Prove that, for every $h\in\mathbb{C}$ and every admissible $a$, the pair $(\sigma_0(q,h), \sigma_1(q,h))$ uniquely determines $q$.
artifact.category_tag: Inverse spectral problems for delay Sturm–Liouville operators
artifact.status_search_result: The Neumann subcase $h=0$ of the Robin-type boundary condition $y'(0)-hy(0)=0$ has been resolved in the negative: a counterexample (an infinite family of iso-bispectral potentials) was constructed for delay $a\in[\pi/3,2\pi/5)$, paralleling the earlier Dirichlet ($y(0)=0$) counterexample. The general Robin case with arbitrary complex $h$ does not appear to have been fully settled; the obstruction noted in the Robin setting (loss of the relation that determines an auxiliary constant from the kernel) means the Dirichlet-style construction does not directly transfer, and uniqueness/non-uniqueness for general $h\neq 0$ remains an outstanding question.

status_evidence.title: On non-uniqueness of recovering Sturm-Liouville operators with delay and the Neumann boundary condition at zero
status_evidence.snippet: A counterexample giving a negative answer for the Neumann subcase (ν=1) of the Robin condition at zero, for delay a∈[π/3,2π/5).
status_evidence.claim: The Neumann subcase h=0 of the Robin-type boundary condition admits an iso-bispectral counterexample, partially answering the question.

status_evidence.title: Inverse problems for Sturm–Liouville differential operators with two constant delays under Robin boundary conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Uniqueness theorems are proven under specific assumptions on Robin-type boundary conditions for delay Sturm–Liouville operators.
status_evidence.claim: Uniqueness results exist for some Robin-type configurations, but the general case raised here is not fully closed.
